s: Which among the following (Provision – Part of the Constitution) is not correctly matched?
o: The Scheduled and Tribal Areas – Part X
x: Tribunals are not mentioned in Part XI but in Part XIV (A). They were inserted in the Constitution by 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 under Article 323-A, which deals with Administrative Tribunals and Article 323-B, which deals with tribunals for other matters. Part XI has various provisions related to the centrestate relations. Hence option (d) is the correct answer.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 323A and 323B (Part XIV-A)?
x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted them, following the Swaran Singh Committee; the 75th Amendment added the rent and tenancy clause.

s: Tribunals are governed under which Part of the Constitution?
x: Tribunals are in Part XIV-A, Articles 323-A and 323-B. Part XIV covers services and Part XI Centre-State relations.

s: What kind of bodies are tribunals in India?
x: Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies set up to reduce pendency in regular courts and bring domain expertise.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about tribunals?
o: They are intended to provide faster adjudication
They bring specialised expertise into dispute resolution
Parent ministries may face a conflict of interest in administering them
They are completely outside the supervisory jurisdiction of constitutional courts
x: Tribunals remain subject to judicial review by the High Courts.

s: On whose advice was Part XIV-A (Articles 323-A and 323-B) inserted in the Constitution?
x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted Part XIV-A on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice.

s: Which Amendment added the rent and tenancy clause to Article 323-B?
x: The 75th Amendment, 1994 added clause (h) on rent and tenancy to Article 323-B.

s: What does Part XIV-A of the Constitution deal with?
o: Services under the Union and the States
x: Part XIV-A covers tribunals; services are in Part XIV, co-operatives in IX-B and Municipalities in IX-A.

s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with relations between the Union and the States?
x: Part XI deals with Union-State relations; Part X deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas and Part XIV-A with tribunals.

s: Who can establish tribunals under Article 323A?
x: Only Parliament can act under Article 323A; both Parliament and States can act under 323B.

s: Which one of the following subjects is associated with Article 323B but NOT with Article 323A?
o: Service conditions in public sector undertakings
Conditions of service of State employees
x: Land reforms are among the subjects listed under Article 323B. Article 323A deals with recruitment and service conditions of public servants.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 323A and 323B?
o: Article 323B permits a hierarchy of tribunals
Article 323A deals with recruitment and service conditions of public servants
Article 323B covers subjects such as taxation, foreign exchange and industrial disputes
Article 323A permits Parliament and State Legislatures to legislate equally
x: Under Article 323A, Parliament alone can legislate.

s: Which Article allows a hierarchy of tribunals (original and appellate)?
x: Article 323-B allows a hierarchy of tribunals; under Article 323-A there is one CAT plus State tribunals with no hierarchy.

s: What principle was laid down in R. Gandhi (2010) regarding tribunal members performing judicial functions?
o: They must be nominated by consumer commissions.
They must be appointed exclusively by the executive.
They must be independent of the executive.
x: R. Gandhi (2010) held that tribunal members performing judicial functions must remain independent of the executive.

s: Which of the following is NOT a merit of administrative tribunals?
o: Compulsory application of the full Civil Procedure Code
x: Tribunals follow natural justice rather than the full Civil Procedure Code; expertise, speed and lower cost are their merits.

s: What is a major criticism of tribunals?
o: Bound by the full Code of Civil Procedure
Run by the ministries whose decisions they review
x: Tribunals are criticised as being run by the same ministries whose decisions they review; low cost, expertise and freedom from the CPC are their merits.

s:
Which of the following statements related to the Central Administrative Tribunal are correct ?

I. It is a statutory body.

II. Its members are drawn from administrative background only.

III. It is not bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure.

IV. Its jurisdiction covers the members of All-India services as well as Central services and Central Government posts.

V. It was set up in 1985.
x: The CAT was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, and covers All-India Services and central government employees. Its members include both judicial and administrative experts.

s: What status is generally given to the Chairpersons of tribunals?
o: Secretary to the Government of India
x: Tribunal chairpersons get High Court judge status. They are not equated with Supreme Court judges, district judges or Secretaries to the Government of India.

s: By which of the following is the Central Administrative Tribunal NOT bound?
x: CAT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it follows natural justice, charges nominal fees and lets parties appear in person.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Clauses excluding the jurisdiction of the High Courts and the Supreme Court in Articles 323-A and 323-B were declared unconstitutional.
The Supreme Court held that tribunal decisions can never be examined by a High Court.
Judicial review under Articles 226/227 and Article 32 was recognised as part of the Basic Structure.
Decisions of tribunals may be scrutinised before a Division Bench of the concerned High Court before approaching the Supreme Court.
x: Option B is incorrect: L. Chandra Kumar struck down the clauses excluding the courts, so tribunal decisions go first to a High Court Division Bench, then to the Supreme Court.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Article 32 is the Supreme Court's review power. Article 323-A covers administrative tribunals, 323-B tribunals for other matters, and 226/227 High Court review.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)?
o: It has original jurisdiction over service matters of Union civil servants
Appeals against its orders go first to a High Court Division Bench
It derives its basis from Article 323A
Appeals against its orders lie directly before the Supreme Court
x: Appeals against CAT orders go first to a Division Bench of the High Court, not straight to the Supreme Court.

s: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) derives its legal basis from which of the following provisions?
o: Article 262 and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 315 and the Central Civil Services Act, 1985
Article 323A and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 323B and the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021
x: CAT is empowered by Article 323A and was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. It is a statutory and quasi-judicial body.

s: Who was the Prime Minister when the Central Administrative Tribunal was set up in 1985?
x: The CAT was set up in 1985 under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. It was not established during Lal Bahadur Shastri's tenure.

s: At what level must Administrative Members of the Central Administrative Tribunal have served?
x: Administrative Members need service at the level of Additional Secretary or above; Judicial Members must be qualified as High Court judges.

s: Of the 69 members of the Central Administrative Tribunal, how many are Judicial Members (including the Chairperson)?
x: CAT has 69 members: 35 Judicial Members, including the Chairperson, and 34 Administrative Members.

s: On what basis does the Central Government establish State Administrative Tribunals?
o: Only on the recommendation of the Supreme Court
Only through a resolution of the State Legislative Council
At the request of the concerned State Government
Automatically in every State under Article 323B
x: A State Administrative Tribunal is set up by the Central Government at the request of the concerned State Government.

s: To which body do appeals lie from the National Sports Tribunal notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025?
x: Appeals from the National Sports Tribunal lie to the Supreme Court.

s: Which Article provides for tribunals for elections and foodstuffs?
x: Elections and foodstuffs fall under Article 323B; Article 323A covers service matters with one tribunal for the Centre and each State.

s: Over the service disputes of which of the following does the Central Administrative Tribunal have no original jurisdiction?
x: CAT covers Central civil servants, AIS officers and civilian defence employees, not private-sector employees.

s: In which year was the Central Administrative Tribunal established?
x: The CAT was established in 1985.

s: Which was the first tribunal set up under Article 323A?
x: The CAT, set up in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, was the first tribunal under Article 323A.

s: From which backgrounds are the members of the Central Administrative Tribunal drawn?
x: CAT has Judicial Members (qualified as High Court judges) and Administrative Members (Additional Secretary or above).

s: Apart from its Principal Bench at New Delhi, how many benches does the Central Administrative Tribunal have?
x: CAT has its main bench at New Delhi and 18 other benches.

s: Which of the following cities does NOT have a bench of the Armed Forces Tribunal?

s: In which year was the Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal, relevant to Andhra Pradesh, set up?

s: Within how many days, an appeal can be made by an aggrieved person by decision of the National Green Tribunal to the Supreme Court?
x: The National Green Tribunal was established on 18.10.2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act 2010 for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to the environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources including enforcement of any legal right relating to environment and giving relief and compensation for damages to persons and property and for matters connected therewith or incidental to it. It is a specialized body equipped with the necessary expertise to handle environmental disputes involving multi-disciplinary issues. The Tribunal shall not be bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but shall be guided by principles of natural justice. The Tribunal has the power to review its own decisions. If this fails, the decision can be challenged before the Supreme Court within ninety days.

s: Which of the following cities has a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?

It upheld all provisions re-enacted by Parliament without modification.

s: Which case held that tribunals could replace High Courts as an effective substitute?
x: S.P. Sampath Kumar (1987) let tribunals replace High Courts; L. Chandra Kumar (1997) overruled it, holding that tribunals only supplement them.
